page.overview:
Who is Bactrosaurus?

is a genus of herbivorous dinosaur that lived in China during the late Cretaceous around 70 million years ago. Bactrosaurus is one of the earliest known hadrosaurid. It was a very early ancestor of Lambeosaurus, another duckbill. Like its relatives, Bactrosaurus was a plant-eater that had many hundreds of teeth, long back legs and short front legs, and a beak on the front of its mouth for cutting and tearing tough plants.

Bactrosaurus was more powerfully built than most other hadrosaurs and was very heavy for its size. It almost appears to be a transitional animal linking iguanodonts with hadrosaurs, and researchers have noted that it almost looks more like an iguanodont than a hadrosaur.

Bactrosaurus is mentioned in the entry of Archaeornithomimus and Gigantoraptor.
